title: Breaking-change checks
bridge: Each breaking-change check is like tsc failing when you remove an export other files import. Except: the importers are outside the PR (the published SDK, on-prem clients, yesterday's pods). So each check builds the old version from the merge base and compares.
intro: Agents will change serializers, migrations and protos. Lesson p10-5 explained what oasdiff, the migration linters, buf and the SDK smoke test compare. This lesson builds the four CI steps in fcp, line by line. They are Python and YAML because they check fcp's Django backend in its own CI.

picture.caption: Four contracts, four checks, one shape: old version, new version, compare.

nodes.label: PR changes cloud or common code
A person records a deliberate break

steps.text: git merge-base HEAD origin/main finds the old version
the export script runs on both trees; oasdiff compares the YAML
lintmigrations and sqlmigrate look only at migrations added since the base
the released rhino-health wheel calls this commit's API over HTTP
a deliberate break needs a line with a ticket key in a protected ignore file

sections.h: Who is on the other side
p: The cloud API has readers outside the PR: the rhino-health SDK on PyPI, the frontend and the MCP server. Customers keep old SDK versions for months. The gRPC protos are read by on-prem clients that upgrade later than the cloud. A migration runs while old pods still serve requests.
G7 adds one check per contract: G7-11 (OpenAPI), G7-15 (migrations), G7-19 (protos) and G7-21 (the SDK). Each one also gets one line in Nova's checking guide (G4), which says when to run it.
Every job that needs the merge base sets fetch-depth: 0 on checkout, because CI checkouts are shallow by default.

callout.text: Agents never change the checks they are judged by. A deliberate API break is recorded by a person in openapi-breaking-ignore.txt, a protected path. Migration exceptions are added by a person, with a comment.

sections.h: oasdiff, part 1: the job and its env (G7-11)
p: First a script, cloud/rhinoCloud/scripts/export_openapi.py. It calls django.setup(), then drf-spectacular's SchemaGenerator(patterns=_MAIN_SCHEMA_PATTERNS, api_version="v2") from rhinoDjango/urls.py. Those are the same patterns /docs/v2/openapi/ serves. It prints the schema as YAML, and does the same for _CONNECT_SCHEMA_PATTERNS.
The export must need no database. If a serializer queries at import time, fix the serializer; do not add a database to this job.
sections.because: We run this job only on branches, because main has no merge base to compare with except itself.

code.text:
openapi-diff:
    name: OpenAPI breaking changes
    runs-on: fcp-runner-set
    needs: check-changes
    if: github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' && needs.check-changes.outputs.has_changes == 'true'
    env:
      ENV: QA
      DJANGO_SECRET_KEY: rhino
      DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE: rhinoCloud.rhinoDjango.settings
      # ...plus whatever settings.py reads at import time (copy from the `test` job); no database is used
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: cloud/rhinoCloud
        run: uv sync --frozen --no-install-project && echo "$PWD/.venv/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

sections.h: oasdiff, part 2: two exports and one compare
p: A git worktree is a second checkout of the same repo in another folder. The job checks out the merge base into $RUNNER_TEMP/base. Then this commit's export script runs twice: once with PYTHONPATH pointing at the base tree, once at this tree. So the very first run of the check already has a base to compare with.

oasdiff runs from its Docker image, pinned by digest. --fail-on ERR fails the job on an error-level change; warnings show as annotations on the PR. A deliberate break is a line with the ticket key in cloud/rhinoCloud/openapi-breaking-ignore.txt, which oasdiff reads with --err-ignore.
sections.because: We run this commit's script against both trees, because the base commit may not have the script yet.

code.text:
- name: Export the v2 schema for the merge base and for this commit
        run: |
          git worktree add "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" "$(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)"
          # This commit's export script runs against both trees, so the first run already has a base.
          PYTHONPATH="$RUNNER_TEMP/base/cloud:$RUNNER_TEMP/base/common" python cloud/rhinoCloud/scripts/export_openapi.py > "$RUNNER_TEMP/base.yaml"
          PYTHONPATH="$PWD/cloud:$PWD/common" python cloud/rhinoCloud/scripts/export_openapi.py > "$RUNNER_TEMP/head.yaml"
      - name: Fail on breaking changes
        # $RUNNER_TEMP sits on the work volume the dind sidecar shares; pin the image by digest
        run: >
          docker run --rm -v "$RUNNER_TEMP:/work" -v "$PWD/cloud/rhinoCloud:/cfg:ro" tufin/oasdiff@sha256:<digest>
          breaking /work/base.yaml /work/head.yaml --fail-on ERR --format githubactions
          --err-ignore /cfg/openapi-breaking-ignore.txt

p: Two tools check each migration added since main. django-migration-linter catches changes that break code still running during a deploy, such as dropping a column old pods read. Squawk reads the SQL from manage.py sqlmigrate and warns about locks and table rewrites on a live Postgres.

Add django-migration-linter to the test dependency group, and to INSTALLED_APPS only when RHINO_IS_RUNNING_UNIT_TESTS=1 (in settings_test.py). The step goes into the test job after "Check for missing migrations"; that job already has the Postgres service sqlmigrate needs. .squawk.toml at the repo root sets pg_version 17.6 and assume_in_transaction = true, because Django wraps migrations in a transaction. It lists excluded rules with a reason each.
sections.because: We start with continue-on-error for two weeks, so the guild sees real findings before the step blocks anyone.

code.text:
# After "Check for missing migrations". This job's checkout needs `fetch-depth: 0` for the merge base.
      - name: Lint new migrations (django-migration-linter + Squawk)
        working-directory: cloud/rhinoCloud
        continue-on-error: true  # advisory for the first 2 weeks, then remove this line
        run: |
          base=$(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)
          ./manage.py lintmigrations --git-commit-id "$base"
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/sql"
          new=$(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=A "$base" -- rhinoCore/migrations/ | grep -E '/[0-9]{4}_[^/]+\.py$' || true)
          for file in $new; do
            name=$(basename "$file" .py)
            ./manage.py sqlmigrate rhinoCore "$name" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/sql/$name.sql"
          done
          if [ -n "$new" ]; then
            # .squawk.toml at the repo root: pg_version, assume_in_transaction = true, excluded rules with reasons
            uvx --from squawk-cli squawk --config ../../.squawk.toml "$RUNNER_TEMP"/sql/*.sql
          fi

callout.text: Client migrations (rhinoAgent, rhinoRawDataHandler) run on customer machines at upgrade time. Leave them out for now; add them later if the guild wants it.

p: The cloud dispatches agent calls by method name: AgentRpcRequest.method_name, field 2 of the proxy proto. So a renamed RPC still parses on the wire and still breaks every client that has not upgraded. buf.yaml picks the rule set that catches that.

In the cloud-ci.yml lint job, which already runs the protoc drift check, set fetch-depth: 0 and add bufbuild/buf-action with setup_only: true. Then run: buf breaking common --against ".git#ref=$(git merge-base HEAD origin/main),subdir=common".
sections.because: We put the module root at common/, because make protoc uses common/ as its proto path.

code.text:
# Module root is common/ because `make protoc` runs with --proto_path=common, so buf sees
# fcp_common/rhinoAgentRpc/*.proto with the same paths as the generated _pb2 files.
version: v2
modules:
  - path: .
breaking:
  use:
    # PACKAGE, not WIRE: AgentRpcRequest carries the RPC by method_name, so deleting or renaming an RPC
    # breaks older on-prem clients even though the bytes still parse. Clients upgrade later than the cloud.
    - PACKAGE
  except:
    # We never use the proto JSON mapping between cloud and client (gRPC binary only). Confirm with the BE guild.
    - FIELD_SAME_JSON_NAME

notes.text: Why common/ is the root: the protoc Makefile's ROOT_DIR is common/, so paths match the generated _pb2 files.
The buf configuration format.
One module: this folder, common/.
The settings for buf breaking.
WIRE allows deleting or renaming an RPC, because old bytes still parse. Our method-name dispatch cannot survive that.
Stricter rules: no removed or renamed messages, fields, services or RPCs within a package.
Rules we turn off, each with a reason.
Cloud and client never use the proto JSON mapping, only gRPC binary. Confirm this with the BE guild.

callout.text: The protos have no reserved entries today. Add a note to common/fcp_common/rhinoAgentRpc/README.md: when you remove a field, reserve its number and name instead of reusing them. A deliberate break needs a person and a plan for old clients.

sections.h: The published SDK, part 1: install and log in (G7-21)
p: Customers run the wheel on PyPI, not the SDK folder in the repo. G7-21 runs a few real SDK calls from the latest release against this commit's API, over real HTTP. pytest-django's live_server fixture starts a server thread on a random port over the test database.

The API Tests job reads the latest version from https://pypi.org/pypi/rhino-health/json and runs uv run --group api-tests --with rhino-health==$SDK_VERSION pytest tests_api/sdk_smoke -m sdk_smoke. cloud/rhinoCloud/pyproject.toml sets exclude-newer = "7 days", which also applies to --with. Override it for this step, so yesterday's release is tested too.
sections.because: We skip the module when rhino_health is missing, because only this CI step installs the released wheel.

code.text:
"""The latest *published* rhino-health SDK against this commit's API, over real HTTP (pytest-django live_server).
The API Tests job runs: uv run --group api-tests --with rhino-health==$SDK_VERSION pytest tests_api/sdk_smoke"""

import pytest

rh = pytest.importorskip("rhino_health")  # in no uv group on purpose: CI installs the released wheel

pytestmark = [pytest.mark.sdk_smoke, pytest.mark.django_db(transaction=True)]  # live_server needs committed rows


@pytest.fixture
def sdk(live_server, builder):
    site = builder.site()  # a fake workgroup and user, created through the API
    session = rh.login(username=site.email, password=site.password, rhino_api_url=f"{live_server.url}/api/")
    return session, site

Import rhino_health, or skip every test in this file when it is missing.
Marks for every test in the module: sdk_smoke, and django_db with transaction=True.
A fixture that needs the live server and the builder from lesson g7-3.

The released SDK logs in over HTTP to this commit's API at the live server's URL.
The test gets the SDK session and the site.

callout.text: live_server runs in another thread, which cannot see rows inside the test's open transaction. transaction=True makes pytest-django commit rows and clean up by truncating tables instead.

sections.h: The published SDK, part 2: one real call
p: The first test creates a project and finds it by name. Add more calls only for what customers use most, picked with the SDK owner. Also test the oldest SDK version we still support; the SDK owner decides which one.
sections.because: We import the SDK's own dataclass inside the test, because the module may be skipped and the import must not run then.

code.text:
def test_published_sdk_creates_and_finds_a_project(sdk):
    from rhino_health.lib.endpoints.project.project_dataclass import ProjectCreateInput

    session, site = sdk
    project = session.project.add_project(
        ProjectCreateInput(name="SDK smoke", description="", type="Validation", primary_workgroup_uid=site.workgroup_uid)
    )
    assert session.project.get_project_by_name("sdk smoke").uid == project.uid  # the name search ignores case


# Next: data schemas, datasets and code objects, picked with the SDK owner from what customers call most.

quiz.q: Why does the oasdiff job run this commit's export script against the merge-base tree too?

options.text: Because the base commit may not have the script yet, so the first run still has a base.
options.why: PYTHONPATH points the same script at the old code.

options.text: Because the base tree's script would give a different YAML format.
options.why: The format is the same; the problem is that the old tree may not have a script.

options.text: Because oasdiff can only read files from the same folder.

quiz.q: An agent renames the RPC HealthCheck to CheckHealth in the onprem proto. Old bytes still parse. Why must buf fail?

options.text: Because buf fails on any change to a proto file.
options.why: buf allows compatible changes, such as a new optional field.

options.text: Because the cloud dispatches by method_name, so older clients do not know CheckHealth.
options.why: That is why buf.yaml uses PACKAGE, not WIRE.

options.text: Because the generated _pb2 files were not committed.
options.why: That is the protoc drift check's job, not buf's.

quiz.q: Why does the SDK smoke test use django_db(transaction=True)?

options.text: Because the SDK writes directly to Postgres.
options.why: The SDK talks HTTP to the live server, never to the database.
It is slower: tables are truncated after each test.

options.text: Because live_server serves from another thread, which cannot see uncommitted rows.
options.why: Committed rows are visible to the server thread.
